arxiv-2103-00129.title: Music Genre Bars
arxiv-2103-00129.creator: Swaroop Panda, Shatarupa Thakurta Roy
arxiv-2103-00129.description: Abstract Music Genres, as a popular meta-data of music, are very useful to organize, explore or search music datasets. Soft music genres are weighted multiple-genre annotations to songs. In this initial work, we propose horizontally stacked bar charts to represent a music dataset annotated by these soft music genres.

arxiv-2201-11610.title: Cycles in Mallows random permutations
arxiv-2201-11610.creator: Jimmy He, Tobias Müller, Teun W. Verstraaten
arxiv-2201-11610.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jimmy He, Tobias Müller, Teun W. Verstraaten. We study cycle counts in permutations of 1 , … , n 1,\dots,n drawn at random according to the Mallows distribution. Under this distribution, each permutation π ∈ S n \pi\in S_{n} is selected with probability proportional to q inv ⁡ ( π ) q^{\inv(\pi)} , where q > 0 q>0 is a parameter and inv ⁡ ( π ) \inv(\pi) denotes the number of inversions of π \pi .

arxiv-2307-16403.title: Spin decoherence in VOPc@graphene nanoribbon complexes
arxiv-2307-16403.creator: Xiao Chen 1,2 , James N. Fry 1 and H. P. Cheng 1,2,3
arxiv-2307-16403.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xiao Chen 1,2 , James N. Fry 1 and H. P. Cheng 1,2,3. Carbon nanoribbon or nanographene qubit arrays can facilitate quantum-to-quantum transduction between light, charge, and spin, making them an excellent testbed for fundamental science in quantum coherent systems and for the construction of higher-level qubit circuits. In this work, we study spin decoherence due to coupling with a surrounding nuclear spin bath of an electronic molecular spin of a vanadyl phthalocyanine (VOPc) molecule integrated on an armchair-edged graphene nanoribbon (GNR).

arxiv-2311-02959.title: Manageable to unmanageable transition in a fractal model of project networks
arxiv-2311-02959.creator: Alexei Vazquez
arxiv-2311-02959.description: Abstract Project networks are characterized by power law degree distributions, a property that is known to promote spreading. In contrast, the longest path length of project networks scales algebraically with the network size, which improves the impact of random interventions. Using the duplication-split model of project networks, I provide convincing evidence that project networks are fractal networks.

arxiv-2411-19721.title: Scaling Methods To Estimate Macroscopic Fundamental Diagrams in Urban Networks with Sparse Sensor Coverage Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2411-19721.creator: Nandan Maiti, Manon Seppecher, Ludovic Leclercq
arxiv-2411-19721.description: Abstract Accurately estimating traffic variables across unequipped portions of a network remains a significant challenge due to the limited amount of sensors-equipped links, such as loop detectors and probe vehicles. A common approach is to apply uniform scaling, treating unequipped links as equivalent to equipped ones, which leads to a strong bias in MFD estimation.

arxiv-2501-06543.description: Abstract . We investigate the incompressible inhomogeneous magnetohydrodynamic equations in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} , under the assumptions that the initial density ρ 0 \rho_{0} is only bounded, and the initial velocity u 0 u_{0} and magnetic field B 0 B_{0} exhibit critical regularities. arxiv-2502-20517.description: Abstract . This is the first of three papers motivated by the author’s desire to understand and explain “algebraically” one aspect of Dmitriy Zhuk’s proof of the CSP Dichotomy Theorem. In this paper we study abelian congruences in varieties having a weak difference term.

arxiv-2509-13329.title: An open-source heuristic to reboot 2D nesting research Journal: European Journal of Operational Research
arxiv-2509-13329.creator: Jeroen Gardeyn, Greet Vanden Berghe, Tony Wauters
arxiv-2509-13329.description: Abstract 2D nesting problems rank among the most challenging cutting and packing problems. Yet, despite their practical relevance, research over the past decade has seen remarkably little progress. One reasonable explanation could be that nesting problems are already solved to near optimality, leaving little room for improvement. However, as our paper demonstrates, we are not at the limit after all.

arxiv-2509-21210.title: Next-Generation Aerial Robots—Omniorientational Strategies: Dynamic Modeling, Control, and Comparative Analysis Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2509-21210.creator: Ali Kafili Gavgani, Amin Talaeizadeh, Aria Alasty, Hossein Nejat Pishkenari, Esmaeil Najafi
arxiv-2509-21210.description: Abstract Conventional multi-rotors are under-actuated systems, hindering them from independently controlling attitude from position. In this study, we present several distinct configurations that incorporate additional control inputs for manipulating the angles of the propeller axes. This addresses the mentioned limitations, making the systems "omniorientational".

arxiv-2602-02774.title: AmharicStoryQA : A Multicultural Story Question Answering Benchmark in Amharic
arxiv-2602-02774.creator: Israel Abebe Azime, Abenezer Kebede Angamo, Hana Mekonen Tamiru, Dagnachew Mekonnen Marilign, Philipp Slusallek, Seid Muhie Yimam, Dietrich Klakow
arxiv-2602-02774.description: Abstract With the growing emphasis on multilingual and cultural evaluation benchmarks for large language models, language and culture are often treated as synonymous, and performance is commonly used as a proxy for a model’s understanding of a given language. In this work, we argue that such evaluations overlook meaningful cultural variation that exists within a single language.

arxiv-2602-15529.title: Tight Communication Bounds for Distributed Algorithms in the Quantum Routing Model
arxiv-2602-15529.creator: Fabien Dufoulon, Frédéric Magniez, Gopal Pandurangan
arxiv-2602-15529.description: Abstract We present new distributed quantum algorithms for fundamental distributed computing problems, namely, leader election, broadcast, Minimum Spanning Tree (MST), and Breadth-First Search (BFS) tree, in arbitrary networks. These algorithms are (essentially) optimal with respect to their communication (message) complexity in the quantum routing model introduced in Dufoulon, Magniez, and Pandurangan [PODC 2025].

britannica-1911-smith-george-philanthrop.title: Smith, George (philanthropist) (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-smith-george-philanthrop.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-smith-george-philanthrop.description: Article 'Smith, George (philanthropist)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. English philanthropist, was born near Tunstall, Staffordshire, on the 16th of February 1831. His father was a brick maker, and when nine years old George Smith was working thirteen hours a day in the brick fields. Nevertheless he contrived to obtain some education, so that in time he improved his position, becoming manager of a brick and tile works.

pmc-10667100.description: Artificial intelligence as a medical device is increasingly being applied to healthcare for diagnosis, risk stratification and resource allocation. However, a growing body of evidence has highlighted the risk of algorithmic bias, which may perpetuate existing health inequity. This problem arises in part because of systemic inequalities in dataset curation, unequal opportunity to participate in research and inequalities of access.

pmc-11444562.title: Prompt response to rituximab in a patient with resistant polymyositis with complications of dysphagia and dysphonia: a case report
pmc-11444562.creator: Yousef Mahmoud Nimer Habes, Saif Ibraheem Mohammad Sadeh, Layth Jamil Mohammad Saada, Ali Jamil Ali Mali, Mohammed Abdulrazzak, Saed I Y Attawna
pmc-11444562.description: Introduction and importance:Polymyositis is an inflammatory process, primarily affecting proximal muscles, characterized by elevated muscle enzymes and distinctive electromyography patterns.Case presentation:The authors present a case of a 33-year-old male patient experiencing complications of polymyositis, including pharyngeal and laryngeal involvement leading to dysphagia and dysphonia. Steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy proved ineffective.

pmc-11481723.title: Comparison of proximal gastrectomy and total gastrectomy in proximal gastric cancer: a meta-analysis of postoperative health condition using the PGSAS-45
pmc-11481723.creator: Xiangyu Yang, Zhili Zeng, Ziyue Liao, Caiyu Zhu, Hongyang Wang, Haijuan Wu, Shu Cao, Weizheng Liang, Xiushen Li
pmc-11481723.description: PurposeProximal gastrectomy (PG) offers advantages over total gastrectomy (TG) in enhancing the postoperative nutritional status of patients with proximal gastric cancer (PGC), yet its effect on long-term quality of life is still debated. This study aims to thoroughly compare postoperative health condition outcomes between PG and TG.

pmc-11684339.title: Genetically predicted immune cells mediate the association between gut microbiota and autoimmune liver diseases
pmc-11684339.creator: Jikang Zhang, Yiqi Hu, Jin Xu, Hua Shao, Qingping Zhu, Hao Si
pmc-11684339.description: BackgroundIncreasing evidence suggests an association between gut microbiota and Autoimmune Liver Diseases (AILDs). However, causal inference remains controversial due to confounding bias in observational studies. Additionally, there is currently no clear evidence indicating that immune cells act as intermediate phenotypes in the pathogenesis of AILDs.

pmc-12538752.title: Healthcare leaders and professionals’ perspectives of the ICON programme to prevent abusive head trauma in infants: a qualitative study
pmc-12538752.creator: Julie M Brose, Julie Mytton, Mark D Lyttle, Maria Theresa Redaniel, Jelena Savović, Hugh McLeod, Carlos Sillero Rejon, Joni Jackson, Maria Barnes
pmc-12538752.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAbusive head trauma (AHT) in infants is the most common abusive injury in young children, and increased awareness has resulted in the development of prevention programmes. Most research evaluating AHT prevention programmes report parental and carer perspectives. Little is known about barriers and facilitators to adopting, implementing, and maintaining educational programmes from the perspectives of managers and staff delivering the education.
